history.dynasty: Cholas (9th century masonry structure); later expansions by the Vijayanagara rulers and the Thanjavur Nayaks (16th century)
history.summary: A Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified in the 7th-century Tevaram by the Nayanmar saint Appar (counted among the 127 southern-bank Cauvery temples), and the largest and one of the oldest Shiva temples in Kumbakonam. The moolavar is a unique conical Shiva lingam, believed to have been fashioned by Shiva himself from nectar of immortality mixed with sacred sand during the mahapralaya (cosmic deluge) - the town's name derives from kumbha (pot) and konam (angle), referring to the tilted pot of nectar whose contents flowed through its nostril-like opening (Tirukudamookku). The present masonry structure was built by the Cholas in the 9th century, with later expansions under the Vijayanagara rulers and the Thanjavur Nayaks of the 16th century. The 30,181 sq ft complex has three concentric compounds and four gopurams, the eastern tower rising 128 ft in 11 tiers. Notable features: the 16-pillared Vijayanagara-period hall with all 27 stars and 12 zodiacs carved in a single stone, five silver-plated festival chariots, a stone nadaswaram, and a six-handed Subramanya idol. Carnatic composer Purandara Dasa visited and composed a song to Kumbeswara. Administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of Tamil Nadu.

name: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple
town_description: Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district on the Cauvery river about 40 km from Thanjavur and 273 km from Chennai, is a historic temple town famed for its Mahamaham festival (held every 12 years) and dense cluster of Shaivite and Vaishnavite shrines.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport (TRZ), about 100 km away, is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Kumbakonam Junction (KMU), about 2 km from the temple, on the Chennai-Tiruchirapalli line.
travel.road: Well connected by road to Chennai, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur, Madurai, Bengaluru and other south Indian cities; the temple is in the heart of Kumbakonam town (Hajiyar Street, Valayapettai), easily reached by auto, taxi or town bus.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; February-March for Masi Magam. The Mahamaham festival occurs once every 12 years.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00-9:30 PM (per casualwalker); six daily rituals run from 5:30 AM to about 9:00 PM - verify before visiting.
